sections.text: The Vital Forces, the Major stars, Fire, Earth, Air, Sky, Sun, Heaven, Moon and Planets; the Angels, the Guardians of the Universe, the divine Healers, the Winds, the Fathers, the Heavenly Singers; and hosts of Mammon-worshippers, demons as well as saints, are amazed.
Seeing Thy stupendous Form, O Most Mighty, with its myriad faces, its innumerable eyes and limbs and terrible jaws, I myself and all the worlds are overwhelmed with awe.
When I see Thee, touching the Heavens, glowing with colour, with open mouth and wide open fiery eyes, I am terrified. O My Lord! My courage and peace of mind desert me.

We have completed chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, and well now be discussing chapter 11, Vishwarupadarshan, the cosmic form of the Divine. In the last chapter, Arjuna had asked Krishna: tell me how I should feel your presence, the presence of the divine, the presence of that all-pervading self, and how I can meditate upon that. In response, Bhagavan gave him various examples of excellence in this world from various walks of life -- applicable to Arjuna and also to us -- showing that from our day-to-day life, from our cultural backgrounds, from our spiritual quest, we find examples all around us of excellence and can feel the Lords presence.
As we discussed in chapter 10, anytime I see excellence, my mind recognizes it as Gods blessings, the grace of God. In other words, divinity is evident in excellence. Bhagavan gave various examples for Arjuna and said, when you see this, it will remind you of my presence in all things and beings.
Im not limited to those excellent manifestations, but thats where you will find it easier to experience my presence. And now that Arjuna has heard that, he says: Im still not experiencing that oneness, the oneness which you talk about throughout this discourse. I have intellectually appreciated it and come to the conclusion that thats what it is -- that there is one singular entity pervading this entire universe, which is you, the Supreme self.
But I need to have that experience. I would like to experience that oneness. This, is similar to how we scientifically make any concept or theory our own knowledge.
First I need to gather all the evidence and data. And then, once I have gathered all the data and evidence, I need to demonstrate that the phenomenon exists. I gather all information about how water is formed.
In chemistry class, two molecules of hydrogen and one molecule of oxygen can create water. But at some point, I want to see the demonstration -- in the lab, I create that situation and then see how hydrogen and oxygen create water. In a similar fashion, Arjuna has now understood, but he wants to see a demonstration.
So the chapter starts with Arjuna Vacha. Arjuna said: Mat Anugraha Ya Paramam Guhyam Adhyatma Sangnitam Yat Tvaya Uktam Vachasthena Moho Ayam Vigato Mama. With your compassion for me, you have given me this secret knowledge.
And as you have said, the self is indestructible, imperishable. One who considers himself to be the slayer or the slain -- in both cases, he is wrong. There is nothing to grieve over in the changes which take place in this world, including death, because death is not the end of existence.
It is only the end of existence in the form of this body. So Moho Ayam Vigato Mama -- by this discourse of yours, you have given me the secret knowledge. Bhavapyayo Hi Bhutanam Shrutao Vistaraso Maya Tvattah Kamala Patraksha Mahatmyam Api Cha Avyayam -- I have also heard the origin and destruction of beings, O lotus-eyed Krishna, from you, and also your inexhaustible greatness.
I heard the greatness of the self, the supreme Brahman, that which is not limited by anything. And therefore my delusion is gone. I understand it clearly now.
Evam Etat Yatha Attha Tvam Atmanam Parameshwara Drashtum Icchami Te Rupam Aishwaram Purushottamam. However, I would like to see that form as you described yourself -- that oneness in this world of plurality. I have understood that you pervade the entire universe and therefore there is no existence separate from you.
However, at this time I cannot see that, and I would like to see that. I would like to experience that oneness of yours. Manyase Yadi Tat Shakyam Maya Drashtum Iti Prabho -- if you think it is possible for me to see that divine form, then, O Lord of Yogas, show me that imperishable form which includes everything in this world.
I would like to see that complete form of yours where everything is in yourself. It is easier for me to see your presence in this world of plurality. It is easier for me to see gold in gold jewelry.
I can take one look at it, experience the gold in it, then pick up another piece. As long as the excellence is there, in other words, the gold is apparent and not covered by something -- the gold is manifested in the jewelry -- I can see the gold in it. So it is easier to see the divinity in the world of plurality for us.
What is not possible for us generally is seeing all the plurality in that one single entity. I can imagine that God is in you. God is in me, God is in He, God is in she.
If my mind and intellect has achieved that level of purity, level of understanding, then I start seeing the divinity in all beings. And therefore, in our culture, when we meet each other, we say, namaste, Namah te, I bow down to you. Im not bowing down to the limited self which is standing in front of me.
Because I may have my own opinion about that person, but I still do. Namaste to all of the people I meet, at least culturally. Thats what we should be doing or we are doing.
Who we are bowing down to is the divinity in that person that I recognize. The divinity in me and divinity in you is the same. So I respect the divinity in you.
I bow down to you with that recognition. My transaction with you would be always of very friendly, very congenial, and not adversarial. Because I have recognized that myself and yourself has one thing in common, that consciousness, the divinity which makes me who I am.
The same divinity, the same consciousness is within you. What I have trouble imagining or perceiving or seeing is that the whole divinity is one, and you and I are in it. And we have heard in Bhagavad Gita before, Bhagavan says, I am not in them, they are in me.
The car is in the space, the space is not in the car. When I see a car which was built in Germany, there was space inside. When it was in Germany, there was German space.
And they seal it tight and then transport that car to United States. Now the car is here, the space is still intact which was sealed in Germany. Now, whether the space now in the United States is the German space or American space in the car, obviously the answer is simple.
The space inside the car is American space. So what happened to the German space which was in the car when it was still tight in Germany? The answer obviously is in our way of seeing space. As long as I see the space in the car, I have difficulty imagining what happening to that space which was German space.
When it came to America, the space was inside the car. Car was never opened till it came here. Well, it should have been a German space in it.
But if I start seeing that the space was not in the car, the car was in the space, then I do not have any difficulty. Car was traveling in the space. And therefore wherever the car is, that country space is in that car, because car is traveling in the space.
For me to imagine that, I have to first have a perception of a space as a totality without any gap. A German space is one space, an American space is another space, I will have difficulty. But if I can imagine a homogeneous, continuous, universal space, now I can see everything is in it.
So what you and I have difficulty in recognizing the unity between myself and yourself and herself, and also the objects in this room is because of the distance between us. I am here and you are there, you are there and she is somewhere else. What is separating us from each other is the space.
What is separating me from my father is the time. My father lived up to 1975 and Im here today in 2014 thinking about it. So we are separated from each other by time.
So there are two things which creates this world of plurality for me, and that is space and time. We have also heard from sages and scientists that this concept of space and this concept of time is creation of my mind. So one can say, well, what is the distance between here to D.C.
And so on. So its too long a journey. And somebody will say its too close, its only two hour drive.
So my mind creates the valuation whether its too far or too little, that the conception of space in my mind, same thing. If somebody says Ill be back in half an hour, well, is it too soon for me or too long for me? I cant wait for half an hour. You need to be back here in 10 minutes.
Because my conception of time is different than his conception of time. For him half an hour is too short, and for me half an hour is too long. Well, anytime somebody goes to India for a vacation and when they come back, and if I ask that person, so how was your vacation? The answer is it was great, but it was too short.
And I say, how long were you there? He said four weeks for me, too long a time. I only go there for a week or two. So for me a two weeks vacation is good enough for them four weeks is too short, because when you are enjoying their four weeks seems too short.
But if you were suffering because of the heat or monsoon and all the other things which we normally complain about, if Im suffering. Ill say, boy, it was too long when I tried. And then I finally was ready to get out.
So even time is a concept of my mind. If these two concepts of my mind are wiped out, then I will see the world completely differently. If the concept of space is wiped out from my mind, then I will see you and I and everyone in this room come together as one entity.
There is no space between us. We are all joined together and we will be one entity with different limbs, but we are all together. Good analogy in his commentary.
There is a toy maker making toys from clay. And he has various toys and various dolls. Elephant, tiger, baby and a bird.
And then he decided, no, this is not good. I need to use this clay for something much larger, more sellable. He takes all those dolls and compresses them into one ball of clay.
And when he compressed them together, what he has done is taken all the space away from each other. Previously they were sitting on a table or in a display box as separate entity. Once he gathers them and lumps them into one.
And now a big lump of clay. At the same time, I can see the face of the elephant on that surface of that lump. Also see the baby smile.
Also see the tigers face. What is taken away from each other is the space. The same way the events in my life has a time value of it was in my past, or it is in my present, or it will be in my future.
My childhood is in my past. My youth is in my past. My old age is in my present.

In these verses, Arjuna witnesses hosts of beings - Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, divine healers, the Winds, demons and saints alike - all gazing at the cosmic form in amazement. Then comes a shift: Arjuna begins to feel overwhelmed and terrified. Seeing the stupendous form with myriad faces, innumerable eyes and limbs, and terrible jaws, he confesses: I am terrified. My courage and peace of mind desert me. The vision that began with wonder now reveals its awe-inspiring and fearsome aspect.
This is a crucial teaching about spiritual growth. We often approach the divine expecting only comfort, beauty, and peace. But the complete vision includes what we might call the terrible aspects - destruction, death, the dissolution of everything we hold dear. Arjuna wanted to see totality, and totality includes both creation and destruction, both the pleasant and the fearsome. His terror is the natural response of the ego when it confronts something that completely transcends its capacity to control or even comprehend.
Today, reflect on what aspects of reality you resist seeing. Do you avoid thinking about death? Do you turn away from suffering in the world? Do you prefer a nice spiritual path without difficult truths? Arjunas experience suggests that mature spirituality requires facing the full picture - not just the comforting divine but also the destroyer, not just light but also the consuming fire. Ask yourself: What would it mean to accept that the same consciousness that creates also destroys? That the God you pray to for protection is also the power behind everything that threatens you? Sitting with this paradox, without resolving it too quickly, is itself a spiritual practice.
